description: WAVE A part 2 of 3 — move the AUTO-GENERATE-ON-SAVE fill server-side (the collection_jobs queue). THIS IS THE CRITICAL PART the user stressed: the order must not break and nothing must double. Today runOneJob in collectionQueue.js consumes a client-filled filled_base64 (browser fills via docxFill.js + qrCode.js in Home.jsx fillDocxForQueue). The user wants the FILLING moved off the browser while preserving the EXACT order: generate the document (fill -> PDF) -> then template+message -> then it goes out (WhatsApp + email), with no breakage and no double-send. Design: instead of the browser filling and sending filled_base64, the enqueue stores only references (the row is already the source of truth per P0-03), and runOneJob dispatches a Render job that FILLS the template (using FEAT-002's renderer) then converts to PDF, returning the PDF bytes; the Worker writes R2 + generated_files (unchanged trust boundary), THEN triggers WhatsApp then email in the SAME order. QR generation moves off the browser too (decision below). This lets filled_base64 stop being stored in D1 (closes M-38 storage hog + #364 failed-job retention gap). EVERY collection_jobs invariant must be preserved: P0-03 enqueue authority (derive year/recordId/payload from the stored collections row, never the client), P0-04 exact-state claim (<iso>#<uuid> token + re-read), attempts/claimed_at/done/failed/retry, on-demand drain throttle, retention sweep, and the new-entry-only WhatsApp+email gate.
steps: Prove-first: capture the CURRENT end-to-end behaviour of the auto-generate path as the behavioural baseline. Extend/read the existing collection-queue tests (p0-collection-claim-atomicity.test.mjs, p0-collection-enqueue-authority.test.mjs, c2-convertdocx-authorization.test.mjs, h10-m38 + pr48 retention) and add assertions that pin the ORDER runOneJob performs its steps (PDF generation, then WhatsApp trigger, then email trigger) and that a NEW entry sends exactly ONE WhatsApp + ONE email, an EDIT sends none, and the same job never double-runs (existing claim tests). This is the anti-double-send / anti-reorder harness that must stay green after the rewrite.

Decide QR placement and justify it. Recommended: generate the QR server-side WITHIN the fill step on Render (Render fills the template, so it has the placeholder set; add a QR generator to server-render — a Node qrcode lib producing the same data-URL publicRecordUrl(recordId) the browser produced). The recordId is DERIVED server-side (P0-03) so the QR encodes the authoritative record URL, not a client-supplied one. Confirm the exact publicRecordUrl format from mgmt/frontend/src/qrCode.js and reproduce it. Alternative to evaluate: Worker generates QR before dispatch and passes it in the fill data — reject-with-reason if not chosen (the Worker has a subrequest/CPU budget and QR is pure compute better placed on Render alongside the fill).

Add a `docx_render` (fill -> PDF) job kind: it must fit the byte contract or extend it on BOTH sides with the drift test still passing. A single auto-generate document is one filled .docx out + one PDF back, well under MAX_ITEM_BYTES(2MB)/MAX_OUTPUT_ITEM_BYTES(4MB); confirm a single-doc render fits the EXISTING contract so no contract change is needed — if the template+image pushes an input over a cap, extend renderContract.js + batchContract.js identically and keep render-batch-contract.test.mjs green. Register the kind in server-render HANDLERS (routes/jobs.js) and in the Worker KINDS set (renderJobs.js). Decide whether docx_render is VERSION_BUMPING (it writes generated_files, so YES — add it to VERSION_BUMPING_KINDS) and whether it is NON_RECONSTRUCTABLE (its dispatch payload carries template bytes + data, not stored in D1, so YES — add to NON_RECONSTRUCTABLE_KINDS so a reconcile does not re-run it and double-write).

Template resolution: Render has NO D1 and cannot read docx_templates. Decision (justify in comment): the WORKER resolves the template via the existing getDocxTemplate (Drive + 7-day KV cache on the Worker side) and sends the template BYTES in the Render dispatch payload, along with the fill data (placeholders incl the server-generated QR if QR is Worker-side, or the QR is generated on Render). This preserves the KV cache (Worker-side) and avoids giving Render a second Drive lookup path for templates. Confirm the template bytes + data fit the byte contract for a single render.

Rewrite the enqueue + runOneJob flow in collectionQueue.js: (a) enqueue no longer requires/stores a client filled_base64 — the row + docType + derived recordId are enough (KEEP P0-03: derive year/recordId/payload from the stored collections row; KEEP the QUEUEABLE_DOC_TYPES whitelist and the derived-recordId match check; KEEP the double-submit NOT EXISTS guard). (b) runOneJob, when there is a document, resolves the template (Worker KV/Drive), dispatches the docx_render job (fill+PDF+QR on Render), and on the callback the Worker writes R2 + generated_files (via an applyDocxRenderResult side-effect mirroring applyPdfConvertResult — base64-STRIPPED stored result, bump data version), THEN triggers WhatsApp then email in the SAME order and same new-entry gate, email still isolated in its own try/catch. PRESERVE P0-04 exact-state claim + token re-read. Because the fill now happens async on Render, ensure the WhatsApp/email steps run AFTER the PDF exists (they need publicLink) — i.e. sequence them on the render callback, not before it, so the generate->message->send order the user requires is guaranteed and nothing sends before the document exists.

Stop storing filled_base64 in D1 for the new path (closes M-38 + #364). Keep the column for backward compat with any in-flight rows, but the new enqueue writes '' for it. The retention sweep (retention.js boundedBlank) then becomes a no-op for new rows (blanking '' is harmless) — confirm h10-m38-indexes-and-retention.test.mjs and pr48-retention-additions.test.mjs STILL PASS unchanged (they test the sweep mechanics, which remain valid). Note the MAX_QUEUE_BASE64_CHARS cap is now moot for new rows but leave it for any legacy client still sending bytes during rollout, or remove it and update Home.jsx accordingly — coordinate with FEAT-004's frontend change.

Update the frontend (Home.jsx fillDocxForQueue + the enqueue call, ~lines 138-233, and the Svelte Home.svelte equivalent) to stop filling in the browser: it now sends the reference-only enqueue (docType, rowIndex, year — NO filledBase64/fileName built in-browser). KEEP the existing inline convertDocxToPdf fallback ONLY if it still makes sense; if the fill is fully server-side the fallback path (which also fills in-browser) should be removed or repointed — decide and justify so the browser no longer needs docxFill.js/qrCode.js for the auto path. Ensure the mgmt/frontend main-chunk budget (230kB, currently ~218.33kB) is not exceeded — removing the in-browser fill should REDUCE it; confirm docxtemplater/qrcode can drop from the auto path.

Mutation-test: (a) swap the WhatsApp and email order and confirm the order test fails; (b) make runOneJob send the message BEFORE the PDF callback and confirm a test catches a message going out without/before the document; (c) make the enqueue trust a client-supplied year/recordId and confirm the P0-03 authority tests fail; (d) weaken the claim to the old pending-OR-processing predicate and confirm the P0-04 double-run/double-send test fails. Record any equivalent mutants with reasons.
Commit on a feature branch (e.g. wave-a2-autogen-serverside-fill). Do NOT push. This PR depends on FEAT-002 being merged (the Render renderer).
acceptance_criteria: The auto-generate path no longer fills the .docx in the browser: enqueue is reference-only and Render performs fill -> PDF via the docx_render job kind (FEAT-002 renderer).
runOneJob preserves the exact order generate document -> WhatsApp -> email, with WhatsApp+email running AFTER the PDF/publicLink exists; a test pins this order.
No double-generate and no double-send: existing P0-04 claim-atomicity and enqueue double-submit tests stay green, plus a test asserting one WhatsApp + one email per NEW entry and none for an EDIT.
P0-03 enqueue authority preserved: year/recordId/payload derived from the stored collections row; the authority tests stay green.

docx_render fits the byte contract (or extends it on both sides with render-batch-contract.test.mjs still passing); registered in server-render HANDLERS and Worker KINDS, added to VERSION_BUMPING_KINDS and NON_RECONSTRUCTABLE_KINDS with justification.
Only the Worker writes R2 (Render returns bytes); template bytes resolved Worker-side (Drive + KV cache) and sent in the dispatch; Render never touches D1 or R2.
filled_base64 is no longer written to D1 for new jobs; h10-m38 and pr48 retention tests still pass unchanged.
mgmt/frontend main chunk stays under 230kB (should shrink); the browser auto path no longer depends on in-browser docxFill/qr.
cd mgmt/backend && npm test and cd mgmt/server-render && npm ci && npm test both pass.
Mutation checks recorded for order-swap, send-before-generate, client-trusted-payload, and weakened-claim.
verification: cd mgmt/server-render && npm ci && npm test
cd mgmt/frontend && npm ci && npm run build (confirm main chunk < 230000 bytes)
